clues: This seaside town sits on the coast of England. It stands where the Humber river flows into the sea.
Rain falls here less than in most places. Its yearly rainfall is among the lowest in the British Isles.
People have lived here since the 6th century. Fishing was its first trade, long before holiday crowds came.
In 2021, its beach earned high praise. A train company ranked it second best among seaside spots trains can reach.
This town stands on the prime meridian line. The line is also called the Greenwich meridian.
